name: How does the Denver climate affect interior trim and molding?

mainEntity.name: How does the Denver climate affect interior trim and molding?

acceptedAnswer.text: The dry climate and seasonal humidity swings across the Denver metro area cause interior framing and trim wood to expand and contract significantly. In winter, heated indoor air dries out timber, often leading to separated miter joints, cracked caulk lines, or loosened nails. When installing or repairing trim in Denver homes, proper acclimation of wood materials before installation, combined with high-flexibility acrylic latex caulking and secure fastening into studs, prevents gaps from opening during winter dry spells.
acceptedAnswer.description: Low humidity and seasonal shifts cause wood to shrink and expand, making proper material acclimation and flexible caulking essential to prevent separated joints.
